terms.gloss: a saint; a woman saint, sāncta
evidence: Vulg. Ps. 30 (31), 24: omnēs sānctī ejus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically the adjective, holy; the Church’s noun for a saint. As a title, Sānctus Petrus, Saint Peter.

evidence: Vives, Exercitātiō 7: trānscurre ad Dīvī Petrī, “run over to St Peter’s”
terms.comment: Classically a god or a deified emperor (dīvus Jūlius); the humanists’ word for a saint.

phrases.latin: Cōnfiteantur tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua, et sānctī tuī benedīcant tibi.
phrases.english: Let all your works give thanks to you, Lord, and let your saints bless you.

phrases.latin: cum ad memoriās sānctōrum, sīcut in Āfricā solēbat, pultēs et pānem et merum attulisset atque ab ōstiāriō prohibērētur
phrases.english: when she had brought porridge, bread and wine to the shrines of the saints, as she used to in Africa, and was stopped by the doorkeeper

sources: Lewis & Short: sanctus · Lewis & Short: divus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. saint.
